Optimal.Notes: A 7 W TDP cap is more than sufficient to hold a rock-solid 60 fps at native 1280x800 with all settings at maximum; the GPU clock can be left on automatic since the game is not GPU-bound. This is the recommended everyday profile for most players.

profiles.Summary: Hades runs excellently on the Steam Deck, being a 2D-style indie action game with very modest PC requirements that the Deck handles with ease at native resolution and high settings. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, and ProtonDB reporters consistently report a smooth, trouble-free experience out of the box.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very lightweight PC requirements (GTX 960-class minimum GPU, 4 GB RAM) and the Deck's RDNA 2 hardware. On your first run, confirm the frame counter stays at your chosen cap in the busiest rooms (Elysium arena fights) — if it does, you can safely lower the TDP further in the Max Battery profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: Hades is extremely light on the GPU; a 5 W TDP and a locked 400 MHz GPU clock are more than enough to hold a steady 40 fps at native resolution. Drop the TDP further to 4 W if you want even longer sessions — the game will still hold 40 fps comfortably.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Hades is not demanding enough to benefit from removing the TDP cap beyond what the Optimal profile already achieves; the game is capped at 60 fps by its own design, so uncapping the frame limit and TDP simply ensures there is zero headroom pressure during hectic combat rooms. Battery life is shorter with no TDP limit, so the Optimal profile is preferable for most sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Full native resolution at maximum quality settings holds a rock-solid 60 fps well within a modest TDP; this is the sweet spot for enjoying the game's gorgeous art at its best.

profiles.Summary: Hades is a 2D action roguelite with very modest PC requirements, running beautifully on the Steam Deck at a locked 60 fps with plenty of headroom to spare. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support and runs natively well under Proton with no significant issues reported.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very low PC requirements (2D/light 3D engine, GTX 960-class minimum) and the Steam Deck hardware. On your first run, verify the 90 Hz cap holds during hectic multi-enemy rooms, and drop to the Optimal profile if you notice any dips.

MaxBattery.Notes: Hades is extremely light on GPU; a 4 W TDP and low GPU clock easily sustain 40 fps. This profile maximises session length for long runs without any perceptible input lag or stuttering.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Hades is light enough that the OLED Deck can push a steady 90 Hz at max quality; the higher refresh rate makes the fast-paced combat feel noticeably snappier on the OLED panel.
